Robots for CT-guided needle insertion: clinical implementation and future perspectives.
desc: [Japanese journal of radiology] Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System
desc: Telephone triage is a safety critical task: from a brief intake note, a nurse must decide whether a caller needs an ambulance, an emergency department, an appointment, or self care at home. Queried directly, large language models (LLMs) are unreliable: they over-escalate routine cases and cannot justify their recommendations against an auditable clinical standard. We present the Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System (ALLMTS), which grounds every disposition in the same commercially maintained telehealth guidelines nurses use. Rather than asking an LLM to triage, ALLMTS makes it execute the guideline: it selects the appropriate guideline and evaluates its triage assessment questions. The disposition follows deterministically from the first positive answer, using the same traversal rule a nurse follows. We evaluate ALLMTS on 566 synthetic, expert-validated scenarios spanning 14 dispositions and designed to test specific guideline questions. ALLMTS achieves 0.95 accuracy, compared with 0.47 for a raw-LLM baseline. On a curated 50-scenario subset released as an open benchmark, ALLMTS reaches 0.98 accuracy, on par with the 0.944 correct disposition rate that a five nurse expert panel recorded on those same scenarios. Critically, on that subset the baselines have over-triage rates of up to 0.50 (0.44 on the full dataset), whereas ALLMTS reduces the over-triage rate to at most 0.02 while maintaining low under-triage. These results support coupling LLM language understanding with executable clinical guidelines for triage from intake notes.

Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Surgical Planning in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.
source: PubMed · Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America
desc: [Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America] Virtual surgical planning (VSP) has transformed oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS) by enabling patient-specific planning and execution of complex procedures using patient-specific surgical guides and implants. Three-dimensional computer-aided design and manufacturing have advanced the field from traditional model surgery to fully digital workflows. These technologies have significantly improved outcomes across a wide range of procedures, including orthognathic surgery, maxillofacial reconstructive surgery, temporomandibular joint surgery, trauma management, and implantology. This article reviews the historical evolution of VSP in OMFS, current major clinical applications, developments in artificial intelligence, and the limitations and future directions of virtual surgical workflows.

title: Sam-Correction: Fully Adaptive Label Noise Reduction for Medical Image Segmentation
desc: The quality of the teacher label has a dramatic impact on the outcome of the machine learning process. Medical image segmentation often suffers from a noisy ground truth (GT) mask due to difficulties in consistent annotation. Although a recent study has proposed a promising method to curate the noisy GT mask, this requires additional well-curated GT masks that are not always accessible without the aid of multiple medical experts. As an alternative, we propose SAM-Correction, which utilizes a foundation model to correct the noisy GT mask in a fully adaptive manner instead of manually preparing well-curated masks. In our approach, we progressively mitigate label noise via the segment anything model (SAM), where prompts are given from another segmentation network that we train concurrently. Experiments with various types of label noise derived from actual human annotations demonstrate that SAM-C achieves precise noise reduction and high-performing segmentation models trained thereby. Our method paves the way for robust model training even when clean labels are entirely unavailable.

Artificial intelligence in gamma knife radiosurgery: applications in treatment planning, response prediction, and toxicity assessment.
desc: [Journal of neuro-oncology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being developed across the Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) workflow, but its current applications and readiness for clinical integration remain underutilized. This narrative review examines the emerging role of AI in GKRS, with emphasis on treatment planning, outcome prediction, and post-treatment assessment. A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was conducted through September 20, 2026 to identify studies applying learning-based AI approaches specifically to GKRS. Eligible studies evaluated AI models using GKRS clinical, imaging, or treatment-planning data, while non-GKRS and non-learning-based studies were excluded. Included studies were synthesized according to major stages of the GKRS workflow. AI applications were identified across tumor segmentation, isocenter selection and treatment planning, prescription and dose-distribution prediction, synthetic computed tomography generation, and plan-quality assessment. Post-treatment applications include longitudinal tumor monitoring and prediction of response, functional outcomes, and toxicity including peritumoral edema and radiation necrosis. Several models demonstrate promising performance, but the evidence remains predominantly retrospective and task-specific, with frequent reliance on single-center or small datasets and limited external or prospective validation. AI has the potential to improve the consistency, efficiency, and personalization of GKRS by supporting specific technical and clinical decisions. Further multicenter validation, prospective evaluation, workflow integration, and demonstration of meaningful clinical benefit are required before routine adoption. AI currently remains a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for radiosurgical expertise.

title: Understanding Communication Failures in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
desc: Multi-agent LLM systems aim to improve reasoning through debate, evidence sharing, and mutual correction, but interaction can also introduce failures that final accuracy alone cannot explain. Agents may converge too early, ignore dissent, suppress correct minority answers, or preserve a wrong framing across rounds. We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks. Using this taxonomy, we analyze failure distributions across datasets and system designs, round-level error dynamics, recovery hardness, majority transitions, minority-signal suppression, and self-reported confidence. We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses. Based on these findings, we recommend stronger disagreement handling, evidence verification, minority-signal preservation, and recovery checks before finalization.

Computational Peptide Design: Emerging Concepts in Antibiotics, Immunity, and Evolution.
desc: [Annual review of microbiology] Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover "encrypted" peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure-activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of "encrypted immunity," in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.

title: Beyond Heuristics and Commercial Navigation: An AI-Augmented Decision-Support for Ambulance Travel Time Estimation
desc: Accurate ambulance travel time estimation is critical for emergency medical dispatch, yet existing decision-support practices often rely on static lookup tables or simplified assumptions regarding how ambulance travel time differs from ordinary passenger-car travel. For instance, they assume ambulances simply travel a fixed percentage (e.g., 5%) faster than ordinary passenger cars. However, such assumptions are rarely validated using real ambulance operational data and may fail to capture the effects of trip priority, temporal context, and origin-destination. We address these limitations using historical ambulance trips from the Skåne region in Sweden. Our analysis reveals that ambulance travel times vary substantially by hour, day, and trip priority, and that commercial navigation systems fail to capture emergency-specific dynamics. We contribute a machine learning system to more accurately estimate ambulance travel time. To make the system interpretable, we explored SHapley Additive exPlanations and permutation importance techniques to ensure that our system captures operationally meaningful patterns.

title: Artificial intelligence and small-business competitiveness in an emerging economy.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are the driving force of developing economies, yet they remain limited in resources to implement artificial intelligence (AI), and there is little empirical evidence that AI adoption is associated with small business growth in the region, particularly in Central Asia. This research makes two contributions. First, we propose a concise framework that links classes of AI technologies to SME competitiveness features and identifies machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI as low-cost, quick-return priority areas for resource-constrained firms. Second, using 16 years of data (2010-2025) for the Bukhara region of Uzbekistan, we estimate ARIMA models for each indicator and forecast eight small business indicators to 2030. Small business output is projected to grow at a steady rate of approximately 16% by 2030, with digital adoption and preferential credit support emerging as indicators associated with long-run growth. Forecast accuracy is high for the human-capital indicator and acceptable for output. The evidence is associational rather than causal: the framework and the forecasts converge on a single, cautiously formulated proposition-the adoption of low-cost AI is measurably associated with the sustainable competitiveness of SMEs, providing a practical, evidence-based starting point for regional AI policy in developing countries.

title: Towards Trustworthy AI-Enabled Emergency Medical Dispatch: Uncertainty-Aware Ambulance Travel Time Estimation
desc: Emergency medical dispatch increasingly relies on AI-enabled decision support systems when making ambulance dispatch decisions. In this process, accurate ambulance travel time estimates are essential for timely resource allocation and prehospital care. However, existing ambulance travel time estimation approaches typically produce only single point predictions. Consequently, they do not indicate how reliable an individual estimate is or how much uncertainty it carries. This limitation is particularly problematic in safety-critical emergency medical service dispatch operations, where trips with similar expected travel times may exhibit substantially different levels of uncertainty. Furthermore, real-world ambulance trip logs may contain domain-specific artefacts, such as co-located healthcare facilities and physically implausible travel speeds. These artefacts can degrade point prediction accuracy and affect the prediction task on which subsequent uncertainty estimation depends. To address these challenges, we propose an uncertainty-aware methodology for ambulance travel time estimation and evaluate it through a retrospective real-world scenario study using two years of ambulance trip data from the Skåne region in Sweden. The proposed methodology moves beyond average-case point predictions by generating context-adaptive prediction intervals with stable empirical coverage across the evaluated operationally important contexts. The resulting prediction intervals provide explicit information about predictive uncertainty that can support more transparent and risk-sensitive ambulance dispatch decision-making.

title: Challenges in AI-based structural modeling of host-pathogen protein interactions.
desc: [Current opinion in virology] Pathogens depend heavily on their hosts, a relationship driven by molecular interactions. Among the diverse molecular classes involved, proteins and protein-protein interactions (PPIs) serve as the pillars of these infectious processes. Driven by opposing natural selection pressures, with one protein adapting to escape the interaction and the other adapting to maintain it, host and pathogen proteins coevolve in this arms race. With the advent of artificial intelligence-driven structural prediction methods, initiated by AlphaFold, highly accurate structural modeling of PPIs has become feasible. Yet, host-pathogen PPIs remain difficult to model with these approaches. In this review, we describe the current state of host-pathogen structural modeling, describe recent studies, and discuss how pushing current methods to their limits might improve success rates.

title: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification
desc: Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising approach to medical image representation learning, yet augmentation strategies of SSL frameworks validated on natural images do not reliably transfer to specialized medical imaging domains. We analyze DINO, a knowledge-distillation based SSL framework, and empirically demonstrate that its default augmentation strategy produces unreliable representations for retinal fundus images, degrading downstream glaucoma classification performance. Guided by the principle that effective cropped views should share minimal redundant information while retaining clinically relevant signal, we redesign DINO's augmentation strategy. Our approach biases the learned representations toward diagnostically critical features rather than low-level image statistics. We evaluate our method for glaucoma classification by training a linear classifier on the frozen representations, achieving strong generalization across seven benchmark datasets. title: Application of interpretable deep learning in brain age prediction: a comprehensive review.
desc: [Reviews in the neurosciences] Brain age prediction has emerged as a promising approach for characterizing interindividual differences in brain aging. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has created a substantial gap between predictive performance and interpretability. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has, therefore, become increasingly important for identifying the neuroanatomical features underlying brain age predictions. This review systematically examines interpretable deep learning approaches for brain age prediction. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect identified 32 eligible studies, which were organized into post-hoc explanation methods and intrinsically interpretable models. We further propose a four-dimensional operational framework encompassing Algorithm Reliability, Robustness and Reproducibility, Biological Validation, and Clinical Utility. The reviewed literature indicates a transition from localized feature attribution toward generative, disentangled, attention-based, and anatomically meaningful representations. However, interpretation remains sensitive to methodological and imaging-related factors, while brain age gap (BAG) is also influenced by age dependency, calibration, reference-population composition, and site heterogeneity. Future research should emphasize standardized evaluation and prospective clinical validation to develop reliable and clinically meaningful brain age biomarkers.

title: OPTARI: An open-source software framework for clinical translation of optoacoustic imaging
desc: Combined optoacoustic (OptA) and ultrasound imaging is a promising modality across a wide range of pathologies. Its use in clinical research, however, is limited by a lack of analysis software accessible to users without programming expertise. Existing tools are either script-based engineering frameworks or proprietary vendor applications. We present OPTARI, an open-source graphical software application to facilitate large-scale clinical optoacoustic-ultrasound (OPUS) studies. OPTARI builds on the napari image viewer and the PATATO toolkit for OptA data processing. It supports native vendor and open HDF5 data formats, aligns with the IPASC standard, and is distributed as a standalone executable. Features include region-of-interest annotation, reconstruction, chromophore unmixing, deep-learning-based tissue segmentation, and temporal and spectral analysis modules. OPTARI offers a combination of features for clinical study analysis that none of the compared tools provide. The automated tissue segmentation produced results comparable to expert labeling for muscle tissue, and batch processing reduced analysis time from minutes to under one second per scan. The tool is used in ongoing clinical OPUS studies. OPTARI connects engineering frameworks with medical research and provides an open-source basis for reproducible and standardized analysis in clinical OptA imaging studies.

title: The Duke Clinically Linked Electrocardiogram and Arrhythmia Repository.
desc: [JACC. Advances] Artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (ECG) algorithms are becoming increasingly powerful tools in the clinical world, allowing for earlier and subclinical detection of ubiquitous and harmful pathologies. However, the strength of these algorithms is directly informed by the strength of the data sets on which they are trained, and there is a growing need for large-scale, diverse, publicly available ECG repositories. The Duke Clinically Linked ECG and Arrhythmia Repository is a large-scale ECG database containing over 5 million clinically acquired ECGs linked to longitudinal clinical data. Its strengths-including demographic diversity, large sample size, linked clinical databases, breadth of represented conditions, access to linked procedure codes, various options for data export, and ease in creating targeted subcohorts-position it as a significant tool in the artificial intelligence-ECG research landscape. This Methods paper outlines the demographics and structure of this database and explores promising research applications of this resource.

title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification
desc: Developing multiple instance learning pipelines for the classification of whole-slide images involves many interdependent design decisions and expertise in both pathology and machine learning. We present AutoMIL, an open-source framework that applies principles from the field of automated machine learning to tackle this task by automating integral pipeline steps, such as preprocessing, training and evaluation. In a benchmark evaluation with default settings, AutoMIL reached ROC-AUC scores of 0.94 on UBC-OCEAN, 0.99 on PCam and 0.93-0.96 on a TCGA-NSCLC subset, comparable to specialised pipelines in related work. Ensembling mainly improved performance on imbalanced data, showing that an automated pipeline must adapt to dataset characteristics. AutoMIL thus provides an accessible baseline for whole-slide image classification without manual pipeline configuration.

title: Decoding Molecular Binding Equilibria through Uncertainty-Aware Memory Retrieval.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] While accurate drug-target affinity prediction accelerates drug discovery, prevailing deep learning approaches are often bottlenecked by poor generalization and an inability to quantify prediction confidence. Here, we introduce CogNet-DTA, a novel memory-augmented framework that synergizes historical binding priors with biophysical constraints. Our approach introduces a Chemical Graph Memory Network that facilitates reasoning by analogy through retrieving canonical binding motifs from historical data. To capture precise structural contexts, we leverage ESM-based evolutionary embeddings combined with Contact-Weighted Attention, which injects ESM-derived residue-residue contact probabilities as spatial biases to refine protein-intrinsic structural context. Distinctively, CogNet-DTA utilizes a Chemo-Geometric Routing Module to organize multimodal inputs into positive and negative predictive pathways under a shared memory prior, providing a conceptual, data-driven decomposition of molecular binding affinity. By integrating Monte Carlo Dropout, our model systematically quantifies uncertainty, providing a critical mechanism to filter out low-confidence, high-risk predictions during virtual screening. Extensive evaluations across diverse benchmark datasets demonstrate that CogNet-DTA achieves highly competitive performance in DTA prediction. Notably, it exhibits robust generalization to novel drugs and targets under strict cold-start and homology-based split settings, successfully mitigating sequence similarity bias.

title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
desc: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

title: Motivation to learn artificial intelligence applications and mental well-being in university students: A cross-sectional study.
source: PubMed · Journal of education and health promotion
desc: [Journal of education and health promotion] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, while students' mental well-being has become a critical concern. The relationship between AI learning motivation and mental well-being was investigated. A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted among 195 students at the Faculty of Education, Najran University, Saudi Arabia, during the first semester of 2025-2026. Data were collected using the motivation to learn AI applications scale and a researchers-developed mental well-being scale (Cronbach's α = 0.792). Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 26 with Pearson correlation, independent samples t-test, and linear regression (P ≤ 0.050). Motivation to learn AI applications showed a significant positive correlation with mental well-being (r = 0.458, P < 0.001). Students with higher motivation reported significantly higher mental well-being (P < 0.001). Female students showed higher motivation (P = 0.007), while no significant gender differences were found in mental well-being (P = 0.421). Motivation significantly predicted mental well-being (β = 0.233, R 2 = 0.184, P < 0.001). Motivation to learn AI applications was positively associated with students' mental well-being and explained a modest proportion of its variance.

title: Automated Nucleus Segmentation in Histology Images: An Attention U-Net Approach with Comprehensive Preprocessing and Inference Pipelines
desc: Objectives: In the area of digital pathology, nucleus segmentation is an essential step for quantitative analysis; however, high nuclear density and staining heterogeneity in histology images pose a great challenge. Methods: This study implements a lightweight Attention U-Net model on the MoNuSeg 2018 dataset to overcome these challenges. The proposed pipeline integrates comprehensive image and mask preprocessing, including stain deconvolution and multi-pass mask smoothing, with a high-fidelity overlapping patch-stitching strategy during inference on high-resolution images. Results: The model achieved an Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 0.8745 on full-resolution, unseen test images. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of attention mechanisms in enhancing feature localization and validates the stitching methodology for generating seamless and accurate segmentation maps. Conclusion: Attention U-Net is an effective and competitive method for automated, scalable nucleus delineation in challenging clinical contexts.

title: Going viral - Virus-targeting nanobodies for research, diagnostics and therapy.
desc: [FEBS letters] The increasing prevalence of viral diseases represents a major threat to global human health, highlighting the urgent need for advanced tools to study viral infections, improve diagnostics, and develop effective antiviral therapies. Antibodies are central to the immune response against viruses and are widely used in research and diagnostics; however, their structural complexity and manufacturing process limit their areas of applications. Single-domain antibodies-better known as nanobodies-derived from heavy chain-only antibodies found in camelids have emerged as a promising alternative. Their unique characteristics-including small size, high stability, the capacity to access cryptic epitopes, and functionality within intracellular environments-make them particularly valuable for viral research. This review highlights recent developments of nanobodies for viral research, diagnostics, and therapeutic applications; discusses their key advantages and limitations; and briefly outlines the emerging role of artificial intelligence-based technologies in facilitating their development to address the expanding burden of viral diseases.

title: Random Jump Forests
desc: Random jump forests are introduced as a nonparametric tool for estimating conditional cumulative transition rates and occupation probabilities in multi-state models. The main idea is that a single tree partitions the covariate space for all transitions simultaneously, using partially observed trajectories, and with Nelson--Aalen estimators at the terminal nodes. Occupation probabilities are recovered through the product integral without requiring the Markov assumption. Uniform consistency and a functional central limit theorem for the estimators of cumulative rates can be established under the assumption that the covariate vector takes finitely many values, and under suitable splitting conditions. In particular, pointwise confidence intervals and simultaneous bands are available in the Markov case. Simulation studies show a predictive accuracy close to the correctly specified benchmark models and marked improvements when benchmarks are misspecified, with further illustration on four biomedical data sets. In the coverage study, confidence bands attain near-nominal coverage in several settings, with pooling of heterogeneous rates being the main source of possible undercoverage. The method, including prediction assessment and variable importance, is implemented in the R package JumpForests.

title: Lightweight open-source reasoning large language model for evidence synthesis screening.
desc: [JAMIA open] To evaluate performance and efficiency of a lightweight open-source reasoning large language model (LLM) against an expert-derived reference standard for screening scientific publication databases. Two expert reviewers screened subsets of database records across 3 stages: (1) base eligibility (n = 200), (2) obesity focus (n = 200), and (3) women of reproductive age focus (n = 150). The LLM (gpt-oss-20b) screened all records (n = 20 118). Performance (F1-score and sensitivity [recall]) and efficiency (average screening rate) were assessed. Interreader agreement was near-perfect ( κ : 0.99-1.00; all P < .001). LLM performance was high: F1-score, 0.83-0.94; sensitivity, 90%-95%; specificity, 86%-99%; accuracy, 89%-94%; precision, 77%-99%; and negative predictive value (NPV), 89%-96%. LLM screening was faster than reviewers (19.4 vs ∼1.0 records/min). The LLM achieved high performance and efficiency relative to an expert-derived reference standard for screening. The use of lightweight open-source reasoning LLMs shows promise to support screening in evidence synthesis workflows.

title: Hyperparameter-Free Boundary-Interior t-vMF Dice Loss for Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Class imbalance and errors near anatomical boundaries remain challenges in medical image segmentation, motivating loss functions that account for these difficulties. Adaptive t-vMF Dice Loss adjusts the similarity function during training but requires hyperparameter tuning. We propose Self-Tuned Boundary-Aware t-vMF Dice Loss (STB-tvMF Dice), which adapts the function separately for boundary and interior regions without tuning shape-adaptation parameters. Each region's shape parameter of t-vMF function is determined from its mean prediction-target cosine similarity in the preceding epoch and remains fixed throughout the current epoch. This rule maximizes the slope of the similarity function at the observed mean similarity, providing a principled basis for adaptation without validation-based parameter selection. Experiments on three datasets and architectures demonstrated its effectiveness. On Synapse with U-Net, STB-tvMF Dice achieved a mean DSC of 70.75%, compared with 63.03% for Adaptive t-vMF Dice Loss. Our code will be available soon.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on students' metacognition: a systematic review.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Given the critical role of metacognition in academic achievement and the rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings, understanding the interplay between the two has become essential. In recent years, a growing number of studies have examined their relationship, creating a pressing need for a systematic review to synthesize the accumulating evidence. This review adhered to the PRISMA guidelines, involving the search and screening of papers from three major databases (Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCOhost). A total of 22 empirical studies were included in the final synthesis. Data extraction and thematic analysis were employed to identify key impacts and underlying interaction patterns. This review distinguishes between Learning-Oriented AI (LAI) and General-Purpose AI (GAI) to organize the evidence. The findings suggest that LAI was more often associated with Guided Interaction, in which AI provides guiding feedback without directly supplying answers, whereas GAI was more commonly associated with Direct Feedback Interaction, in which AI provides answers or explicitly corrects errors. Across both categories, positive findings were reported for several metacognitive outcomes, including regulation, awareness, and shared metacognition. However, some GAI studies also reported that students relied excessively on AI, particularly when they accepted direct answers from AI without sufficient reflection. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of interaction design and teacher guidance in shaping how AI supports students' metacognitive development.

title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
desc: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.

title: An artificial intelligence assisted framework for automated quantified root canal curvature measurement on periapical radiographs.
desc: [Journal of dental sciences] Root canal curvature is a complex anatomical variation that complicates endodontic treatments. Traditionally, dentists rely on two-dimensional periapical radiographs (PA) and manual methods to estimate curvature angles. However, this conventional approach is highly time-consuming and subjective, often leading to inconsistent measurements. This study aims to develop a fully automated, objective framework for precise angular measurement and severity grading of root canal curvature. The YOLO26n-seg model was employed to segment roots and classify single- or multi-rooted teeth from PA. Furthermore, we proposed an image processing algorithm that standardized orientation, extracted centerlines, and applied three-point circle fitting to establish tangential lines for curvature measurement. The framework's performance was validated against a ground truth determined by five experienced dentists. YOLO26n-seg achieved outstanding segmentation precision (98.8%), sensitivity (97.3%), and intersection over union (96.2%). For angular measurement, the framework demonstrated high accuracy with errors of merely 0.7-1.6 degrees compared to manual assessments, yielding a root mean square error of 1.2° and R2 up to 98.9%. Moreover, the automated system reduced average processing time per PA from 39.9 to 70.8 s to just 0.6-1.7 s, an approximately 44-fold increase in efficiency. The proposed automated framework for root canal curvature measurement provides accurate and consistent geometric data, offering robust support for clinical diagnostic needs. By enhancing evaluation efficiency and reducing the diagnostic burden on clinicians, this system serves as a valuable auxiliary tool that further advances the standardization of dental imaging analysis.

title: Introduction to Allergy Modeling Across Species with Ethical and Regulatory Considerations.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Allergic diseases affect the health and quality of life of humans and domestic animals. The prevalence of allergic diseases is increasing and likely associated with changes in climate and lifestyle conditions with decreased exposure to beneficial microorganisms. Animal models include multiple species (e.g., mice, rats, zebrafish, guinea pigs, dogs, cats, sheep, swine, monkeys) that are essential to study the immunological mechanisms of allergic diseases and to evaluate new therapies that can be beneficial for both humans and animals. The animal models contribute to overcoming ethical limitations in human research and have been scientifically validated with the required approval of ethical committees for animal experimentation. The animal models guide allergy modeling with different methods and translational protocols disclosed in the Methods in Molecular Biology book, "Allergic Disease Models: Methods and Translational Protocols".

title: Deep learning-based automated per-tooth detection and segmentation from unretracted smile photographs.
desc: [Journal of dental sciences] Natural smile photographs are universally accessible yet no automated method achieves clinically acceptable per-tooth detection from these images. Existing frameworks require lip-retracted intraoral views, and prior work on smile images achieved insufficient accuracy. This study developed a per-tooth detection and segmentation pipeline for natural smile photographs and assessed its applicability to digital smile design. A total of 1471 smile photographs were annotated via model-assisted labeling. Fifteen You Only Look Once (YOLO) models across three architecture families and five size tiers were compared. A two-stage pipeline combined the best-performing detector with high-quality Segment Anything Model (HQ-SAM) for per-tooth mask segmentation. Segmentation quality was evaluated against manually drawn ground truth on a 75-image subset, and intra-rater reliability was assessed on 20 images. YOLO12x achieved the highest mean average precision (mAP 50-95) of 0.915. YOLO12 variants occupied the top two positions in precision. HQ-SAM segmentation yielded a mean dice similarity coefficient (Dice) of 0.970 ± 0.055 on 709 matched teeth without dental-specific fine-tuning. A domain comparison confirmed that the smile-trained model substantially outperformed a retracted-view model (mean average precision at intersection over union (IoU) 0.50 [mAP50] 0.959 vs 0.600). Per-tooth detection and segmentation from natural smile photographs are feasible using data-efficient fine-tuning on a modestly sized, progressively annotated dataset. The narrow performance gap across model sizes suggests compact variants are viable for resource-constrained deployment. Zero-shot HQ-SAM segmentation achieves strong agreement with manual annotations without dental-specific fine-tuning.

title: Pharmacological Activities, Biosynthetic Strategies, and Future Prospects: A Comprehensive Review of Baicalein.
source: PubMed · Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
desc: [Journal of agricultural and food chemistry] Baicalein, a 4'-deoxyflavone from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, possesses diverse pharmacological activities including antimicrobial, antifibrotic, antiviral, antitumor, and antioxidant effects. Its effective antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties position it as a promising functional food ingredient and nutraceutical candidate. Traditional production via plant extraction is limited by long growth cycles and low yields, while chemical synthesis uses toxic reagents and harsh conditions. Microbial biosynthesis offers a sustainable alternative. To date, baicalein titers of 367.8 mg/L in Escherichia coli and 401.9 mg/L in Pichia pastoris have been achieved through pathway optimization. However, a systematic review integrating its bioactivities and biosynthesis is still lacking. This review summarizes baicalein's sources, structure, pharmacological activities, and applications, with a focus on heterologous biosynthesis and pathway optimization. Future prospects are also proposed to promote its further biomedical applications and efficient production.

title: Deep Learning-Enhanced All-Nanofiber Sensors for Pressure-Temperature Sensing and Stimulus Discrimination.
desc: [Nano letters] Flexible sensors for elderly-assistive robots typically chase high sensitivity, while comfort and multisensory capabilities are largely ignored. Here, we break this pattern with a deep-learning decoupled sensor based on tunable all-nanofiber membranes. Unlike conventional sensors that rely on multiple complex signals, our device uses a single sensing mode and decouples the pressure-temperature signal. The all-nanofiber sensors not only offer excellent pressure-temperature sensing performances but also demonstrate outstanding elderly-friendliness, including biocompatibility, breathability, and degradability. A deep learning algorithm decouples the mixed signals, enabling accurate recognition of liquid temperature and volume in a cup, as well as classification of 15 daily objects during robotic grasping with 97.78% accuracy. This work provides a simple, ecofriendly, and high-performance sensing solution for elderly-assistive robotics and smart home systems.

title: Fine-tuning improves deep learning-based digital phenotyping of lettuce genetic resources.
desc: [Frontiers in plant science] Morphological characterization of agricultural genetic resources relies largely on visual assessment by experts, and applying the same criteria repeatedly to large collections is labor-intensive. Image-based deep learning can support this process, but systematic evidence on training strategies suited to genebank trait data remains limited. This study targeted six morphological traits of lettuce genetic resources characterized according to the test guidelines of the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV). Using genebank images accumulated from 2012 to 2025, six convolutional neural networks were trained with three training strategies under identical conditions, and their performance was compared. Fine-tuning achieved the highest mean macro F1-score in 35 of the 36 backbone-trait combinations and significantly outperformed training from scratch and feature extraction, whereas no single backbone was superior across all traits. Misclassifications were concentrated in morphologically adjacent classes rather than randomly distributed, and for the ordinal traits, errors spanning two or more class levels were rare. These patterns suggest that the remaining classification difficulty was associated in part with the morphological continuity between neighboring classes. The attainable performance also differed among traits, distinguishing traits for which the training strategy alone achieved relatively high performance from those for which it did not. These results provide empirical evidence for selecting training strategies and for determining the role of model-assisted characterization on a trait-by-trait basis in genebanks.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface.
desc: [Science advances] The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning-based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.
